infrastructure/graphiti/ontology.py.group_function: Core schema and type definitions for Graphiti knowledge graph infrastructure enabling structured representation of organizational entities and their relationships.
infrastructure/graphiti/ontology.py.raw_output: This file defines the ontology layer for Graphiti, a knowledge graph system. It contains 8 entity types (Product, Feature, Decision, Issue, Release, Person, Team, Component) and 8 edge/relationship types (WorksOn, Owns, DependsOn, Implements, Blocks, Decides, Mentions, HasFeature). Each class inherits from Pydantic's BaseModel for schema validation. The file exports three configuration dictionaries: DEFAULT_ENTITY_TYPES maps entity class names to their type definitions, DEFAULT_EDGE_TYPES maps relationship names to relationship classes, and DEFAULT_EDGE_TYPE_MAP defines valid entity-to-entity relationship combinations (e.g., Person can WorksOn or Mention a Product). This provides a flexible framework for extracting and organizing organizational knowledge into a typed graph structure."

infrastructure/repositories/data_reposit.overall_summary: Async persistence layer for managing DataRecord and ChunkRecord entities using SQLAlchemy. Provides CRUD operations with tenant and user isolation.
infrastructure/repositories/data_reposit.group_function: Core repository abstraction for data persistence, supporting multi-tenant, multi-user document storage with chunked content retrieval.
infrastructure/repositories/data_reposit.raw_output: DataRepository is the primary persistence layer for the application. It manages DataRecord (document metadata and body) and ChunkRecord (text fragments) entities. The class implements async CRUD operations with SQLAlchemy ORM. Key features: (1) create_with_chunks atomically creates a parent record and adds associated chunk records, (2) list queries records by tenant_id with optional user_id filtering, (3) get retrieves a specific record with authorization, (4) delete removes records with authorization checks. All operations are async and use parameterized queries for SQL injection prevention. Tenant and user isolation are enforced at the query layer.

routers/data_router.py.overall_summary: FastAPI router exposing REST endpoints for data record management, supporting list, retrieve, and delete operations with scope-based access control and Graphiti integration for knowledge graph operations.
routers/data_router.py.group_function: API gateway for data CRUD operations; coordinates between FastAPI request handling, database sessions, and business logic via DataService.
routers/data_router.py.raw_output: This FastAPI router defines three endpoints: GET /data (list records), GET /data/{data_id} (retrieve single record), and DELETE /data/{data_id} (soft/hard delete). Each endpoint depends on scope extraction (tenant/user context) and async database sessions. The DataService orchestrates database queries and Graphiti client interactions. Error handling includes 404 for missing records and 503 for Graphiti failures. The router follows multi-tenant patterns with tenant_id and user_id scoping.

routers/scope.py.raw_output: The file defines a FastAPI dependency endpoint `get_scope()` that parses the X-Scope header to extract tenant_id and user_id from a colon-separated format. It uses the settings module to determine whether to apply default placeholder values when the header is missing or incomplete. The function raises HTTP 400 if required scope information cannot be resolved. This is a critical routing/middleware-like component for multi-tenant isolation.

routers/search_router.py.raw_output: This file implements a FastAPI router for search operations. It defines a single GET endpoint at /search that accepts a required query parameter (min 1 char). The endpoint retrieves a Graphiti client, builds a tenant/user-specific group_id from scope dependencies, instantiates SearchService with that group context, and executes the search. It includes error handling for unavailable Graphiti client and search failures. Dependencies: fastapi, infrastructure.graphiti (client and group_id builder), routers.scope (multi-tenancy scope), and services.search_service (business logic).

It handles CRUD operations (create, read, list, delete) with multi-tenant isolation and transactional bulk ingestion.

services/data_service.py.group_function: Core service layer bridging HTTP/business logic with data persistence and external knowledge graph ingestion; enables multi-tenant document ingest workflows with optional AI enrichment via Graphiti.
services/data_service.py.raw_output: DataService is a stateful service class managing the lifecycle of data records. Constructor accepts AsyncSession, tenant_id, user_id, and optional Graphiti client; instantiates three repository instances. Key methods: create_record (single doc with optional chunking, Graphiti episode creation, error propagation), create_records_bulk (transactional per-file, success/error separation), list_records (tenant/user scoped), get_record (with chunks), delete_record (cascades to Graphiti episodes). Integration with Graphiti is conditional, logged for failures, and uses group_id derived from tenant+user. Chunk indexing preserves document structure via chunk_document utility. All DB operations are scoped to tenant_id and user_id for isolation.

services/search_service.py.overall_summary: SearchService is a thin wrapper around the Graphiti search client that executes semantic searches across grouped knowledge graphs. It transforms Graphiti search results into a standardized payload format containing facts with temporal validity markers.

services/search_service.py.group_function: Service layer for search operations; abstracts Graphiti client complexity and standardizes result formatting for API consumers.
services/search_service.py.raw_output: SearchService wraps the external Graphiti library to provide search functionality. The class accepts a Graphiti client instance and list of group IDs during initialization. The async search() method queries Graphiti with the provided query string and group IDs, then transforms results by extracting fact, valid_at, and invalid_at fields. However, the implementation contains a bug: it builds a payload array but returns the original results instead of the payload. The service serves as an adapter layer between the API layer and the Graphiti search engine, enabling multi-group search routing and result standardization.

infrastructure/repositories/chunk_reposi.raw_output: ChunkRepository implements a persistence layer using SQLAlchemy async session. It provides three core async methods: create_batch (inserts multiple chunks with sequential indices), list_for_data (queries chunks for a data record with tenant/user filtering), and delete_for_data (removes chunks with parent record validation). The class enforces multi-tenant isolation by scoping queries through parent DataRecord entities and optional user_id filters. Dependencies include ChunkRecord and DataRecord models from infrastructure.models, and SQLAlchemy select/delete operations.
